teams.heading: Jake White becomes Fiji's third head coach after Mick Byrne's removal
teams.body: Planet Rugby's analysis of Jake White's appointment starts with a count: he is Fiji's third head coach this year. Mick Byrne, the former head coach, said Fiji wanted to 'move in a new direction', and the union chairman first cited health issues before saying he had been removed. Interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula oversaw defeats to Wales, England and Scotland before the job went to White, whom Planet Rugby calls a gamble.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item that adds a new angle on the appointment, Fiji's coaching churn, rather than repeating White's plan or quotes.

teams.heading: Manny Feyi-Waboso on track for England's Australia test despite hamstring tweak
teams.body: England's game-breaking wing Manny Feyi-Waboso should be fit for the Australia test despite tweaking a hamstring for Exeter against Newcastle on Sunday. Initial scans showed no major damage, and Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter said: "He's had a scan and there's nothing I'm hearing from our physios saying there should be a long-term issue." Feyi-Waboso will miss Exeter's Champions Cup opener at Toulouse on Saturday, with Baxter adding that it becomes a different conversation if he still feels it next Monday.

lead.why: Hard injury news on a key England wing, corroborated across three outlets, and not yet led in this briefing.

teams.heading: France women to meet Lions women in Cardiff in historic first match
teams.body: France women will face the British and Irish Lions women in a historic first at Cardiff's Principality Stadium before the Lions' 2027 tour to New Zealand. Jo Yapp, the Lions head coach, leads a side facing the French, who are ranked fourth in the world. It is only the second meeting between the Lions and France, after the men won a friendly in Paris in 1989. Lions women's committee chair Carol Isherwood hopes for a sea of red in the stadium, not just Wales.

teams.heading: Jo Yapp's Lions Women face France in historic first Test in Cardiff
teams.body: The British and Irish Lions Women will play their first-ever Test against France at Cardiff's Principality Stadium, ahead of their inaugural tour of New Zealand, where they face the Black Ferns. Head coach Jo Yapp said: "There are moments in sport that only come around once and this is one of them." France have finished second behind the Red Roses in each of the past seven Six Nations and reached the 2025 World Cup semi-final, so the Lions have picked a stern opener.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the pack, and it is a hard news announcement about a fixture rather than a retrospective or a repeated Chicago story.

teams.heading: Italy's best world ranking: No. 8, reached in 2007 and 2024
teams.body: Italy's highest world ranking is No. 8, a mark the team has reached in two separate years, 2007 and 2024. Their current Nations Championship record is more modest: three played, none won, three lost, with 37 points scored and 131 conceded in those matches. Their next match is a Round 4 meeting with South Africa, the reigning world champions.

teams.heading: Rory McHaffie, Jamie Stewart and Callum Reidy make Edinburgh and Glasgow debuts
teams.body: Three of Scotland's next generation have made their first appearances for Edinburgh and Glasgow in the United Rugby Championship this season. Rory McHaffie, the Scotland Under-20s winger, came off the bench against Ulster in Belfast before scoring the winning try on his home debut at the Hive against Stormers. Prop Jamie Stewart made his Edinburgh debut in Italy against Zebre Parma, replacing Pierre Schoeman in the 73rd minute, while scrum-half Callum Reidy, Scottish-qualified, debuted in Glasgow's 36-19 win over Connacht. Both clubs remain undefeated in the competition.

lead.why: It is the only genuinely new item in the pack, and it concerns Scotland-qualified players in their first club appearances.

teams.heading: Cardiff's Corniel van Zyl backs Taulupe Faletau to play within weeks
teams.body: Wales number eight Taulupe Faletau is expected to feature before the Nations Championship resumes in November, with Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl saying there are no major concerns over long-term injuries. Faletau was not fielded before last Saturday's Leinster game, the first time since a March shoulder injury, after van Zyl said he felt uncomfortable with his readiness. Asked if he will play in the next couple of weeks, van Zyl said: "I believe so, 100%."

lead.why: A fresh Wales number eight availability story that is not the Thomas item already reported, and it bears on the squad Steve Tandy names next week.

teams.heading: Argentina wore 1986 World Cup football kit replica against England in Santiago
teams.body: Argentina wore a one-off darker blue Le Coq Sportif retro kit with silver numbers in their Round three Nations Championship match against England in Santiago del Estero, copying the strip Diego Maradona wore for the football team at the 1986 World Cup, The Sun reported. The Pumas lost 24-31 that day, and Argentina's own post read: "Memories that span generations and remain alive in the collective memory." The stunt drew heavy attention on social media.

lead.why: The most texted item in the pack about Argentina's own conduct; the other leading candidates have already been reported on this tab.

teams.heading: Mark Nawaqanitawase unavailable for Wallabies' Nations Championship Tests, agent confirms
teams.body: Mark Nawaqanitawase will not play for the Wallabies in their Nations Championship Tests in the UK, according to his agent, Milan Volavola-Shankar, who says Les Kiss, Wallabies coach, was told in July. The winger, who is also eligible for Fiji and Italy, remains open to all options. "Mark will not be available for international rugby this year," Volavola-Shankar told Code Sports. The absence covers the away matches against England, Scotland and Wales.

lead.why: It is hard news on Wallabies eligibility and availability for the UK Tests, which a fan would act on, unlike the pundit takes and the Harry Wilson story already reported.

teams.heading: Japan win three of last five, with September's Fiji win the latest
teams.body: In their last five games, Japan have won three and lost two, and the current run stands at three straight wins. The most recent of those was a 20-15 victory away to Fiji in September, part of the Pacific Nations Cup Knockout Stage. Their last defeat came in Round three, a 15-42 loss to France. Both defeats fall before the current winning run began.

teams.heading: James Parsons wants Timoci Tavatavanawai in All Blacks Bledisloe Test squad
teams.body: Former All Blacks hooker James Parsons wants Timoci Tavatavanawai in the matchday squad for Saturday's Bledisloe Cup Test in Sydney. Rennie has already had to replace four injured players: Asafo Aumua, Anton Segner, Leroy Carter and Ethan Blackadder, calling up George Bell, Du'Plessis Kirifi, Jamie Hannah and Anton Lienert-Brown. On the Aotearoa Rugby Pod, Parsons said: "I'm going to go there again, Tavatavanawai, I just want to see it." Tavatavanawai has only two Test caps since his 2025 debut, despite shining in midweek games on tour.

lead.why: It is the only candidate with hard selection and injury news tied to Saturday's Bledisloe Cup Test, and the pundit's view is attributed to him.

teams.heading: Ivan van Rooyen names 30-man Lions squad for three-week European tour
teams.body: Ivan van Rooyen, Lions head coach, has named a 30-man touring group for their Champions Cup debut against La Rochelle on Saturday and the back-to-back URC matches in Scotland that follow. He plans to use all of them, having watched his side concede nine tries in a 57-15 derby defeat to the Bulls at Loftus that dropped them to seventh on the URC table. "We're going to take 30 guys on tour and hope to use all of them really well and give everyone good minutes," he said.
